web.title: Jodi Pehchano: Kitty Party Acting Pair Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Jodi Pehchano is a kitty party game where ladies find their famous jodi only by acting. Rules, chit list, the Akeli twist, tips and FAQ for 8 to 20 players.
web.intro: Jodi Pehchano is a silent acting game for a kitty party: the host writes famous pairs like Raj and Simran or Chai and Parle-G on chits, tears each chit in half, and every lady gets one half. Without speaking or showing her chit, each lady must act out her word and find the lady holding the other half, and the first pair to show a matching chit to the host wins. The crazy twist is the Akeli chit, which has no pair at all: the lady who gets it wins if she can fool any lady into believing she is her jodi. It needs only paper, a pen, a bowl and a phone timer, and works for 8 to 20 ladies in about 15 minutes.
materials: Paper chits, one per pair, torn in half
A bowl to shuffle the halves
A phone timer set to 2 minutes
A small prize for the winning pair, and one for the Akeli if she wins
steps: Before the game, the host writes one famous pair on each chit, for example Raj | Simran, Jai | Veeru, Chai | Parle-G, Samosa | Chutney, Pav | Bhaji, Chhole | Bhature, Dal | Chawal, Tom | Jerry, Jethalal | Daya and Saas | Bahu, and tears each chit in half between the two names.
If the number of ladies is odd, the host adds one extra chit that says only "Akeli!". If it is even, she also tears one chit into three: Amar | Akbar | Anthony, so the numbers work out.
All the halves go into a bowl and are shuffled. The bowl goes round and every lady takes one half, reads it secretly and hides it in her hand or under her dupatta.

The host starts a 2 minute timer. From now on nobody may speak or show her chit. Every lady acts out her word, sipping invisible chai, dancing like Simran, scolding like a saas, to find the lady with the other half.
When two ladies think they are a jodi, they hold hands and walk to the host together, then show both halves. If the halves match, they are a winning pair. The first matching pair takes the top prize.
The lady with the Akeli chit has no real jodi, so she acts as if she belongs to someone. If any lady walks to the host with her, the Akeli wins and the fooled lady is out.
rules: No speaking, mouthing words or showing your chit. If the host catches you, you freeze for 10 seconds.
A wrong pair at the host goes back and keeps searching; there is no limit on tries until the timer ends.
Any lady who goes to the host with the Akeli is out, and the Akeli wins her own prize.
The first pair to show matching halves wins. Rank the next two pairs for second and third if you like.
variations: As soon as a pair is found, tie their wrists loosely with a dupatta and let them walk around together while the rest search.
In round 2, act only with your face; both hands stay behind your back.
The winning pair must act out a 10 second scene of their jodi before the prize is handed over.
tips: Mix easy and tricky pairs: films, food, TV serials and cartoons all work, and food pairs make the funniest acting.
Write in big letters so every lady can read her half at a glance.
Count the ladies before you tear the chits so there are exactly enough halves, plus the Akeli for an odd number.
Avoid pairs that tease a real lady in the group; keep it to famous names and food.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Jodi Pehchano?
faq.a: It works best with 8 to 20 ladies. Everyone plays at the same time, and a bigger group only makes the silent acting more chaotic.

faq.q: What do you need to play Jodi Pehchano?
faq.a: Paper chits, a pen, a bowl and a phone timer. The host writes famous pairs on the chits and tears each one in half before the game.

faq.q: What famous pairs can you use for Jodi Pehchano?
faq.a: Good pairs are Raj and Simran, Jai and Veeru, Chai and Parle-G, Samosa and Chutney, Pav and Bhaji, Dal and Chawal, Tom and Jerry, Jethalal and Daya and Saas and Bahu.

faq.q: What if there is an odd number of players?
faq.a: Add one Akeli chit with no pair. With an even number, add the Akeli and tear one chit into three, Amar, Akbar and Anthony, so everyone still has a match.

faq.q: Is Jodi Pehchano a good icebreaker for a kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. It gets every lady up and moving in the first few minutes, needs no reading aloud or skill, and new members mix with everyone while they search.
